extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of political science, policymakers and reformers interested in constitutional design and civil service reform
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and practical standards for assessing executive-legislative relations, civil-service organization, and representative bodies' functions (legislation, oversight, transparency). Emphasizes unity of responsibility, distinctions between political and non-political offices, promptness in emergencies, and the role of public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for inefficiency vs impeachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ultimate authority should have the privilege to dismiss for inefficiency; impeachment is aimed above the head of business management and is ill-suited to correct routine folly or incapacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impeachment is ponderous and requires gross offenses and overwhelming indignation to be effective; for everyday administrative incompetence dismissal is "quite as effective" and more merciful. Example: 'A merchant would not think it fair... to shoot a clerk who could not learn the business. Dismissal is quite as effective.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Impeachment as remedy for public crime (limited effectiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Impeachment secures accusation and trial for public wrongs but is a slow, difficult process that seldom acts except in cases of the grossest offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impeachment requires something like passion to set it going; it functions more as an 'empty menace' historically. The House is described as a 'tardy grand jury' and the Senate an 'uncertain court.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity (singleness) of responsibility in executive government
rubrics_metrics.description: Good government requires that ministers be clearly responsible to one master (a single source of political accountability) rather than having divided or ambiguous allegiances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The British civil-service reforms succeeded once Cabinet government made ministers responsible to the Commons alone; this unity of responsibility prompted ministers to pursue merit-based appointment reforms and accept accountability for administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid parceling power that confuses responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Parcelling out authority into small bits (division of powers) tends to make power irresponsible because each actor can shift blame onto others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When responsibility is cut up, officials can plead constraint by committees or other branches; the result is evasions, mutual blaming, and difficulty identifying who should be punished or held responsible for poor outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power must be paired with strict accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Power plus strict accountability are essential constituents of good government; trustees must be empowered but also made clearly answerable for abuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrusting a chief with real power and the potential for ruin (reputation, honor, commercial prospects) furnishes motive to serve. 'Power and strict accountability for its use are the essential constituents of good government.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharp distinction between political and non-political offices
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear line must be drawn between offices that are political (involved in choosing policy) and those that are non-political (administrative), with different rules applied to each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-political offices should be governed by strict business discipline, merit-tenure, and earned promotion; political offices should be subject to party choice. Determining where the line is drawn (e.g., status of Secretaries) is 'the cardinal point of practical civil service reform.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for decisive authority and promptness in emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The constitutional system should provide a supreme or ultimate head able to decide at once with conclusive authority in moments of sudden exigency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without a single head, important steps require consent/cooperation of other branches, producing paralysis in emergencies. Example: wartime necessity required constitutional accommodations to allow prompt action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective oversight, transparency, and public instruction as core legislative functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Aside from lawmaking, a representative body should supervise administration, keep national concerns in broad daylight, and instruct and guide public opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vigilant oversight and public discussion may be as important or more important than legislation. If Congress provided daily knowledge of important transactions, 'their confidence in the executive... would... be established.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and pathologies of committee/investigation powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Congressional investigation is a semi-judicial tool that can expose scandal but is limited and may be indignifying without producing removal or reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committees magnify scandal by cross-examining subordinates and ministers; often offenders remain in office despite shame and public exposure. Committees also fragment comprehension of policy—Congress may follow its committees 'somewhat blindly.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislation tends to beget further legislation; exercise caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation typically generates more legislation, complicating industrial and financial systems and making future regulation and legislative adjustment ever more difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every statute brings lineage and progeny, and as economic organization grows complex, the legislator's task of adjusting rules to avoid harming economic forces becomes harder. Legislators must be mindful that lawmaking can create perpetual work and unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public opinion as both restraint and engine of reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Public opinion provides the salutary fear of accountability that restrains bad practices and can be the force that drives civil-service reform when institutional mechanisms fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Westminster Review quotation: public accusation restrains evil practices and vents peccant humors. In the U.S., reform often arose from persistent public demand placed upon Congress rather than from executive initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointments/dismissals should not be controlled by a third party
rubrics_metrics.description: It is impractical for a principal's chief agent to be appointed by a third party who makes the agent independent of the principal's control; the appointing and dismissing authority should align with who directs policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the chief agent (e.g., a department head) is appointed by and effectively serves Congress rather than the President (or vice versa), coordination and accountability for policy are undermined; the principal must have control over appointments/dismissals for efficient management.
